facts.fact: Zuihoden is Date Masamune’s final resting place on hillside grounds approached by steps among cedar trees.
facts.excerpt: climb up the steps to the quiet hillside grounds of Zuihoden, Date Masamune’s final resting place

facts.fact: The complex includes family burial sites and a museum with excavated objects; it is one developed recommendation, not several stops.
facts.excerpt: includes the burial sites of numerous members of the Date family

facts.fact: Nehanmon is the roofed main entrance with black doors and gilded Date crests.
facts.excerpt: Nehanmon Gate (Nirvana Gate), the main entrance to Masamune’s mausoleum

facts.fact: The present mausoleum is reconstructed; the original was destroyed in World War II.
facts.excerpt: The mausoleum is a reconstruction of the original, which was destroyed during World War II.

facts.fact: Masamune’s excavated items and the successors’ collections are not all in the same museum.
facts.excerpt: Masamune’s burial items are exhibited at the Sendai City Museum, but those of Tadamune and Tsunamune, the second and third lords of Sendai, can be viewed at the Zuihoden Museum.
